title: SilentRetrieval: Hijacking Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Semantically-Preserving Adversarial Data Poisoning

problem.claim: RAG systems can mitigate LLM hallucinations but introduce a critical corpus-integrity vulnerability.

contributions.claim: SilentRetrieval is a two-stage data-poisoning attack that hijacks RAG systems using fluent adversarial documents.
The attack combines Coordinated Beam Search for retrievability-preserving document optimization with Context-Adaptive Trigger Generation for integrating manipulation triggers.
The abstract reports effectiveness across datasets, target LLMs, retrievers, and a Wikipedia-scale poisoning setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Under a one-poisoned-document-per-query evaluation with synthetic target answers, the attack achieves the reported HR@10 and ASR-LLM results on Natural Questions and MS MARCO while maintaining near-benign perplexity.
Cross-model and unseen-retriever transfer tests report nontrivial effectiveness, including 64.7% average HR@10 under the injected-corpus protocol.

A sampled Wikipedia-scale evaluation reports 74.2% HR@10 at a 0.016% poisoning ratio, while human evaluation reports lower flag rates than disfluent baselines but higher suspicion than benign content.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG reduces hallucinations but creates a corpus-integrity vulnerability.
SilentRetrieval is introduced as a two-stage poisoning attack using fluent adversarial documents.
The first stage optimizes retrievability and fluency; the second fuses manipulation triggers into document content.
The attack is evaluated on benchmark datasets, multiple target LLMs, unseen retrievers, and Wikipedia-scale sampling.
Combined defenses reduce attack success but increase latency, and human evaluation finds residual suspiciousness.

source_observation.claim: Poisoned documents can be optimized jointly for retrievability, fluency, and trigger integration.

interpretation.claim: RAG security depends on both retrieval exposure and generation-time manipulation pathways.

application.claim: Assess RAG defenses at both corpus-retrieval and context-generation boundaries.

exception.claim: Defense combinations may substantially reduce attack success while introducing latency costs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify performance on non-synthetic target answers.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or full-text reproducibility information.
